answer: Seat-lottery admission assigns each agent slot by hashing a public beacon with a waiter's earned ticket, so identity multiplication buys no edge. Like a fixed jade marker, each ticket is consumed once and its position on the draw terrace is fixed before applicants commit. An attacker must fund and operate many independently reachable hosts to hold many tickets, paying real bandwidth per attempt, since duplicate hosts collapse into one entry no fable of clones can undo.
